summary: Fail. The Go quota gate is fail-open against the live quota answer. quota.ts:273 reads the week window as windows["week"], but the live OpenChamber /api/quota/opencode-go answer names it windows["weekly"] (night-4.11.sh:75, probe-4.10.sh:56, cron-daily.sh:539, README.md:269). I reproduced the live shape: 5h 10, weekly 100, monthly 10 gives {"state":"ready"}. So the Go 100 % week threshold never fires, and a pass, probe, or judge call can start at weekly 100 %. The same function returns ready when the required 5h or week window is absent (quota.ts:271-279), though spec D15 says a missing field is stopped; I reproduced {"5h":10} -> ready and {"day":10} -> ready. The tests are green (quota 17, review-run 52, judge-run 30) but they fabricate the key "week", so they do not pin the live contract. Provenance: phase_base_sha 57baaaa, role_base_sha 3c4e462, audited_head_sha cc8afbd (current HEAD); audit scope range 66fe1ac..cc8afbd. The Go row key and route name cannot make a non-Go route take the Go thresholds; routes.json is repo-owned and the quota answer cannot set the provider. The 5h threshold works because the live key is 5h; only the week key is wrong. The 80 % stop still holds for every other source. A2 and A6 do not apply.
blocking_findings: B1 [Blocker] harness/model-guide/quota.ts:273 (stateOf :271-279): the Go week threshold reads windows["week"], but the live /api/quota/opencode-go answer names the week window windows["weekly"]. Evidence: night-4.11.sh:75, probe-4.10.sh:56, harness/cron-daily.sh:539, README.md:269 all read weekly. Reproduced: body {"usage":{"windows":{"5h":{usedPercent:10},weekly:{usedPercent:100},monthly:{usedPercent:10}}}} -> {"provider":"opencode-go","state":"ready","windows":{"5h":10,"weekly":100,"monthly":10}}. So the Go 100 % week threshold never fires, and review-run.sh / judge-run.sh start a pass, probe, or judge call at weekly 100 %. This also breaks the between-diff stop (review-run.sh:778-786) and the start test (judge-run.sh:451-460), because both key on QUOTA_STATE=wait. Fix: read windows["weekly"] (keep windows["5h"]); add a Q11 test with the live shape (5h low, weekly 100 -> wait) and one pass, probe, and judge case on the live shape.

B2 [Blocker] harness/model-guide/quota.ts:271-279: the Go branch returns "ready" when a required window is absent. Spec D15 says a missing field is "stopped". Reproduced: {"5h":10} -> ready; {"day":10} -> ready; {"week":10} (5h absent) -> ready. parseAnswer (:228-266) accepts any non-empty window set, so a truncated answer reaches stateOf. Effect: a partial or damaged answer starts a Go pass, probe, or judge call (fail open). Fix: for the Go provider, require windows["5h"] and windows["weekly"] to be finite numbers; if either key is absent, return "stopped". Add Q11 cases: missing weekly, missing 5h, and only day -> stopped.
nonblocking_findings: N1 [Minor] harness/model-guide/review-run.sh:256-264 and harness/model-guide/judge-run.sh:240-245 key the Go rule on quota_source, while quota.ts:271 keys it on the --provider value (quota_provider). They agree in routes.json today, but a future row that sets the two fields differently can drop the 80 % stop. Fix: derive both from one field, or refuse a row whose quota_provider does not map to its quota_source.

N2 [Nit] Test gaps: no case sends a negative usedPercent (quota.ts:258 rejects it, but no test pins it), and no case sends the live "weekly" key. Q9/Q10 (quota.test.ts:487, :512), review G1/G2/G3 (review-run.test.ts:1085, :1126, :1972), and judge G1/G2/G3 (judge-run.test.ts:1615, :1666, :1735) all use the fabricated "week" key. Fix: add the negative and live-shape cases.

Process hygiene: after each of my three gates, pgrep -af "fake-opencod[e]" and pgrep -af "quota-serve[r]" printed nothing (rc 1). At 01:05 my later check saw a transient fake-opencode pair (pid 1796240/1796246, temp /tmp/mg-review-run-SkSrFK) and one quota-server (pid 1796033, temp /tmp/mg-review-fake-RHtsam); both temp folders are not mine, the PIDs are newer than my gates, and they were gone at the next check, so a concurrent session ran the same suite. I did not start or stop them. My manual probes used inline node servers on 127.0.0.1:18641-18644 and I killed each one.

B1 reproduction: inline node HTTP server returned the live shape {usage:{windows:{"5h":{usedPercent:10},weekly:{usedPercent:100},monthly:{usedPercent:10}}}}; npx tsx harness/model-guide/quota.ts --provider opencode-go --base http://127.0.0.1:18644 printed {"provider":"opencode-go","source":"opencode-go","state":"ready","cap":3,"windows":{"5h":10,"weekly":100,"monthly":10}} and EXIT 0.
B2 reproduction: same harness with {"5h":10} printed state ready; {"day":10} printed state ready; {"week":10} printed state ready. All EXIT 0.

Live key evidence: /home/daniebo/.local/share/lending-desk-bench/model-guide/jobs/night-4.11.sh:74-75 reads windows["5h"] and windows["weekly"]; probe-4.10.sh:55-56 is the same; harness/cron-daily.sh:539-540 reads windows.weekly and windows.monthly; README.md:269 names usage.windows.weekly.usedPercent. The live scripts fail closed: an exception or a non-usable value prints fail, and night-4.11.sh:137-139 skips the route.

Go row selection: routes.json has three opencode-go rows with quota_provider and quota_source both opencode-go; review-run.sh:246-264 and judge-run.sh:223-245 read the exact route row and key IS_GO_ROUTE on quota_source. A route name or quota answer cannot set the provider, so a non-Go route cannot take the Go thresholds (audit item 1).

Other sources: review-run.sh:785-789 and judge-run.sh:691 keep the 80 % stop for IS_GO_ROUTE=0; R6 (review-run.test.ts:1025) and J11 (judge-run.test.ts:1546) pin it on kimi-code-plan-cn. Parse validation: quota.ts:259 rejects a null window, a missing usedPercent, a non-number, a non-finite value, and a negative value -> stopped; Q3 pins the string, 1e999, and missing-usedPercent cases.
